tools.name: Claude Native Scheduled Tasks
tools.oneLine: Built-in recurring tasks with push notifications. No code.
tools.best_for: An agent that reaches out on a schedule with zero setup.
tools.watch_out: Needs a paid Claude plan (Pro, Max, Team or Enterprise), with per-plan daily run limits; time can drift at daylight-saving.
tools.history: Proven in the field — powers Eve's 5 PM check-in. Re-checked 28 Aug 2026: still paid-plans-only (Pro 5, Max 15, Team/Enterprise 25 runs a day) and now runs server-side with no device required.

tools.name: Twilio
tools.oneLine: The industry standard for real SMS, WhatsApp and voice.
tools.best_for: When an agent needs to actually text a person, two-way, worldwide.
tools.watch_out: The official Twilio MCP server is read-only — it searches and retrieves API documentation and cannot send a message, place a call, or touch your account. Sending requires your own API integration, or Twilio Labs' experimental twilio-alpha MCP server, which is not covered by Twilio Support and takes account credentials as a command-line argument. US texting needs carrier registration; publicly reported breaches (2022 phishing, 2024 Authy) have since been remediated.
tools.history: Breach history reviewed and judged remediated. Trust held at 5. Re-checked 28 Aug 2026: the official MCP server turns out to be documentation search only (twilio__search / twilio__retrieve), so the official path cannot send — disclosed above. Trust is unchanged; this is a fit limitation, not a safety one.

sources.label: Twilio MCP server docs — read-only search/retrieve

tools.name: Resend
tools.oneLine: Modern, developer-first email with a hosted connector. Nothing to install.
tools.best_for: A clean, modern, agent-ready way to send email.
tools.watch_out: Email only; sending-domain DNS setup takes a few steps.
tools.history: SOC 2 and GDPR confirmed. Free tier steady at 3,000 emails/month. Re-checked 28 Aug 2026: incident sweep found no new material change.

tools.name: Postmark
tools.oneLine: Famous for landing mail in the inbox — use only the official package.
tools.best_for: When reaching the inbox reliably matters most.
tools.watch_out: In Sept 2025 a malicious npm copy named `postmark-mcp` secretly BCC'd every email to an attacker — install only Postmark's own official server (github.com/ActiveCampaign/postmark-mcp). Free tier is 100 emails/mo.
tools.history: Sept 2025: an impostor package was found in the wild. Official package pinned in the catalog. Re-checked 28 Aug 2026: the impostor incident remains as documented by Snyk; no new issue found.

tools.name: SendGrid
tools.oneLine: Huge-scale, battle-tested — but no official agent connector.
tools.best_for: High-volume sending on a proven platform.
tools.watch_out: No official connector that can actually send — Twilio's official MCP server is read-only. sendgrid.com merged into twilio.com in Feb 2026 (branding and docs only; the API, SMTP endpoints and keys are unchanged). The permanent free tier was retired on 27 May 2025 and replaced by a 60-day trial (100 emails/day); not self-serve HIPAA; Twilio has past breaches, since remediated.
tools.history: Downgraded to Caution when the permanent free tier became a trial. Re-checked 28 Aug 2026: the trial still stands. Verdict revised to Trusted on 28 Aug 2026 — the downgrade had been triggered by a pricing change, which the rubric already scores under Cost, and partly by the parent company's breach history, which Twilio's own Trusted entry discloses. sendgrid.com merged into twilio.com in Feb 2026, so the two now share one security page. Every caveat above still stands; what changed is the verdict, not the disclosure.

sources.label: Twilio changelog — SendGrid free plan changes
Twilio SendGrid Email API (sendgrid.com now redirects here)
Twilio MCP server — read-only, search and retrieve only

tools.name: Slack
tools.oneLine: Post an agent's messages, alerts and approvals into channels and DMs.
tools.best_for: Putting an agent's output where a team already works.
tools.watch_out: Internal only; connector needs an internal or listed app.
tools.history: Official Slack-hosted MCP server generally available since 17 Feb 2026 — score raised on reliability. Re-checked 28 Aug 2026: confirmed; Okta access control for the MCP server added Aug 2026.

tools.name: Tavily
tools.oneLine: The search layer most agent frameworks reach for first. Paste one key.
tools.best_for: Searching the web with the least setup and a real free tier.
tools.watch_out: Acquired by Nebius — announced 10 Feb 2026; the service continues under the Tavily brand. Draws on other providers, not its own index.
tools.history: Acquisition flagged at first vetting. Re-checked 28 Aug 2026: confirmed against Nebius's own announcement.

sources.label: Nebius — agreement to acquire Tavily, 10 Feb 2026

tools.name: Exa
tools.oneLine: Its own index, finding things by meaning rather than keywords.
tools.best_for: Finding the exact right thing by meaning, not keywords.
tools.watch_out: Pricier per search; needs a little tuning.
tools.history: SOC 2 and HIPAA confirmed. Well funded; no change since first vetting. Re-checked 28 Aug 2026: incident sweep found no new material change.

tools.name: Linkup
tools.oneLine: Privacy- and EU-minded search, easiest install, most generous free tier.
tools.best_for: EU compliance, privacy, or a bigger free allowance.
tools.watch_out: Youngest/smallest; a little vendor-longevity risk.
tools.history: Keeps no data by default — noted against their SOC 2 report. Re-checked 28 Aug 2026: incident sweep found no new material change.

tools.name: Perplexity
tools.oneLine: Returns ready-made cited answers, not just links.
tools.best_for: Cited, ready-to-use answers with a documented compliance posture.
tools.watch_out: DPA/BAA are Enterprise/sales; US-hosted; self-declared; token pricing. Disclosure: their Comet browser — a different product from this search API — had prompt-injection hijack disclosures in 2026 (Zenity Labs, LayerX), and an unproven class action over data sharing was filed in March 2026.
tools.history: Human-verified 22 Jul 2026: compliance claims read in full and found self-declared. Re-checked 28 Aug 2026: no breach of the search API found; the Comet vulnerabilities and the pending lawsuit are disclosed above for transparency, and concern a separate product.

tools.name: Mem0
tools.oneLine: A ready-to-use memory layer — no database to assemble yourself.
tools.best_for: Giving an agent memory without wiring up infrastructure.
tools.watch_out: Newer company. Their trust centre lists SOC 2 Type 1 — Type II is not shown — and HIPAA as a self-attestation rather than a certification.
tools.history: Audit-in-progress noted at first vetting. Re-checked 28 Aug 2026 against Mem0's own trust centre: SOC 2 Type 1 and a HIPAA self-attestation are listed; Type II still is not. Will re-score when Type II lands.

tools.name: Zep
tools.oneLine: Tracks how facts change, so an agent knows what's true now.
tools.best_for: When facts change over time (preferences, statuses).
tools.watch_out: Small/early-stage; the self-hosted Community Edition was retired in 2025 — open-source work continues as Graphiti.
tools.history: Cost score lowered when the free self-hosted tier was retired. Re-checked 28 Aug 2026: confirmed against Zep's own announcement.

sources.label: Zep — end of Community Edition support

tools.name: Pinecone
tools.oneLine: The most turnkey vector database. Fully managed and certified.
tools.best_for: A rock-solid managed vector store to build memory on.
tools.watch_out: It's a database, not a memory layer; press reports in Aug 2025 said it was weighing a sale.
tools.history: SOC 2, ISO and HIPAA confirmed. Re-checked 28 Aug 2026: no sale announced — the reporting still dates to Aug 2025.

tools.name: Weaviate
tools.oneLine: Feature-rich open-source vector database, strong at scale.
tools.best_for: A feature-rich open-source vector DB, strong at scale.
tools.watch_out: No permanent free managed tier.
tools.history: SOC 2 Type II confirmed. No status change. Re-checked 28 Aug 2026: incident sweep found no new material change.

tools.name: Chroma
tools.oneLine: Confirmed maximum-severity remote-takeover flaw, still unpatched.
tools.best_for: Local prototyping only — use the Rust version, never expose to the internet.
tools.watch_out: NVD rates this pre-login remote-takeover bug 10.0/10 (CVE-2026-45829). Still unpatched — the advisory lists no patched version, and v1.5.9 remains the latest stable release. Use the Rust server; never expose the Python server to the internet.
tools.history: Human-verified 22 Jul 2026 (CVE-2026-45829, CVSS 10.0). Re-checked 11 Aug 2026: v1.5.9 shipped without a fix. Re-checked 28 Aug 2026: still no patch — the GitHub advisory lists “Patched version: None” and 1.5.9 is still the latest stable. Warning stands; re-checking until a patch ships.

tools.name: LlamaParse
tools.oneLine: Turns messy PDFs, scans and Office files into clean text.
tools.best_for: Reading documents reliably with no infrastructure.
tools.watch_out: No free self-host; HIPAA enterprise-only.
tools.history: Generous free tier verified. No status change. Re-checked 28 Aug 2026: incident sweep found no new material change.

tools.name: Reducto
tools.oneLine: Vision-first reader for the hardest files — tables, charts, handwriting.
tools.best_for: Complex, high-stakes documents where accuracy is everything.
tools.watch_out: No free self-host; accuracy scores are vendor-run.
tools.history: SOC 2, HIPAA and private deployment confirmed. Vendor-run benchmarks noted. Re-checked 28 Aug 2026: incident sweep found no new material change.

tools.name: Docling
tools.oneLine: Free, open-source, runs entirely on your own machine.
tools.best_for: Parsing documents privately and for free (needs some code).
tools.watch_out: Not turnkey; needs technical setup.
tools.history: Now under the Linux Foundation — governance risk lowered. Re-checked 28 Aug 2026: governance strengthened further — docling-graph joined the project under LF AI & Data, and IBM and Red Hat launched a DocLang specification working group in June 2026.

sources.label: LF AI & Data — DocLang working group, June 2026

tools.name: Unstructured
tools.oneLine: The broadest range of file types, with dozens of source connectors.
tools.best_for: Pipelines ingesting many file types from many sources.
tools.watch_out: Use the newer 'Transform' connector; HIPAA not listed.
tools.history: Deprecated connector flagged; entry updated to the Transform connector. Re-checked 28 Aug 2026: incident sweep found no new material change.

tools.name: Stripe
tools.oneLine: An official agent toolkit and MCP server, from a heavily-audited processor.
tools.best_for: Handling real payments from a well-audited, widely-used processor.
tools.watch_out: Primarily lets an agent RECEIVE money; agent-spending (Treasury) is still in preview. Toolkit package names are mid-restructure.
tools.history: Published 22 Jul 2026 as the trusted anchor for Payments (PCI L1, SOC 2, ISO 27001). Re-checked 28 Aug 2026: Agentic Treasury is still access-by-request preview, so agent-spending remains preview; the MCP server is hosted at mcp.stripe.com with OAuth.

sources.label: Stripe — Agentic Treasury (preview, access by request)

tools.name: PayPal
tools.oneLine: Official toolkit + MCP across a huge network; does both directions.
tools.best_for: Sending and receiving across a huge global network.
tools.watch_out: In January 2025 New York's Department of Financial Services fined PayPal $2 million over a December 2022 breach that exposed names, Social Security numbers and tax IDs for roughly 35,000 customers; the regulator cited missing multi-factor authentication and rate limiting. Python toolkit support still pending.
tools.history: Published as Caution on the NYDFS enforcement action. Re-checked 28 Aug 2026: confirmed against the regulator's own press release.

tools.name: x402
tools.oneLine: Open HTTP micropayment protocol (Coinbase/Visa/Stripe-backed). Crypto only.
tools.best_for: HTTP-native micropayments between agents and services.
tools.watch_out: Crypto/stablecoin settlement only (no fiat yet). A signature-verification bypass in the x402 SDK (GHSA-qr2g-p6q7-w82m, March 2026) has been patched; per the advisory it affected Solana facilitators and did not put user keys, contracts or funds at risk. Separately, independent research demonstrates five practical attacks on the protocol's authorization, binding and replay handling. Real demand still thin.
tools.history: Published as Caution. Re-checked 28 Aug 2026: the SDK advisory is patched (npm @x402/svm 2.6.0, pip 2.3.0, Go 2.5.0); the remaining findings are design-level and validated academically, which keeps this at Caution rather than Warning.
